simple.meaning: צֶמֶד (tsemed) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a yoke or team (i.e. pair); hence, an acre (i.e. day's task for a yoke of cattle to plough).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 19:3. The surrounding context includes family, family line, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צֶמֶד (H6776) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a yoke or team (i.e. pair); hence, an acre (i.e. day's task for a yoke of cattle to plough)
definitions.usage: acre, couple, × together, two (donkeys), yoke (of oxen).
definitions.full: H6776. tsemed צֶ֫מֶד noun masculine 1Kin 19:19 couple, pair ; — ׳צ construct Judg 19:3 +; suffix צִמְדּוֺ Jer 51:23 ; plural צְמָדִים 1Kin 19:19 ; 2Kin 9:25 (but see below); construct צִמְדֵּי Isa 5:10 (Ges § 93m ); — 1 couple, pair , usually of animals, ׳צ חֲמֹרִים Judg 19:3 , 10 ; 2Sam 16:1 ; בָּקָר ( הַ ) ׳צ span of oxen 1Sam 11:7 ; 1Kin 19:21 , plural of more than one span 19:19 (ploughing), Job 1:3 ; 42:12 ; מְּרָדִים צֶמֶד 2Kin 5:17 ; ׳צ מָּרָשִׁים Isa 21:7 , 9 a pair of horsemen ; plural also of one pair of riders 2Kin 9:25 (but read probably צֶמֶד , so Kit); ׳צ alone = span (of oxen) Jer 51:23 . 2 a measure of land (only square measure in OT) like acre ; originally apparently what a span can plough (in a day; see Now Archaeology i. 202 Benz Archaeology 208 ; compare modern faddan , = what, can be ploughed in a season Schumacher ZPV xii (1889), 163 f. , Across Jordan 22, or in a day Bergheim PEQ, 1894, 192 , Ency. Bib. ACRE ), ׳צ שָׂדֶה 1Sam 14:14 (on text see Dr HPS); צִמְדֵּיכֶֿרֶם Isa 5:10 .
